goal: Issue #690 — reconcile the #664 one-sided grip (G) σ⁺ band scale (a whole-lap pace σ) with the per-CLASS deficit units it is attached to. Planning engagement only; implementation is a later engagement.

questions.question: Is #690's stated premise (σ⁺ = hypot(mu, sigma)) still true in the code, and what is the genuine residual defect?
questions.resolution: PARTLY STALE. Unmerged branch fix/721-grip-band-units already replaces hypot(mu, sigma) with abs(sigma) and drops mu from the signature, because mu is the ~90 s absolute session pace level. #690's headline mechanism is therefore already fixed there. The GENUINE residual defect is the one #690's title actually names: compute_class_utilization_observable computes ONE scalar σ⁺ and hands the SAME whole-lap value to every per-class band, so the (2+k) per-class widths sum to (2+k)·σ_session instead of σ_session — the band on each part is as wide as the band on the whole.

questions.question: What are get_grip_at's units, and who consumes g_sigma_onesided at what grain?
questions.resolution: Units confirmed: both mu and sigma are WHOLE-LAP pace seconds. Consumer topology: producer (class_utilization_observable) → builder script writes the same scalar into every per-class row → store column on driver_class_observables → src/physics/fingerprint/fit.py is the real downstream consumer, aggregating it per (driver, class) cell and composing sigma_cell = sqrt(sigma0² + shared_floor² + g_sigma_onesided² + sigma_lapsampling²). class_utilization_validation.py is NOT a consumer. Because fit.py's cell grain is already (driver, class), a per-class σ flows through it with no code change.

questions.question: Does a per-class quantity that can carry the scaling already exist, and does a per-class σ force a schema change?
questions.resolution: Yes and no. ClassTimeLedger.time_share_by_class already exists: shape (2+k), same W-column order as time_deficit_by_class, sums to 1.0 by construction, derived only from map geometry and one speed profile (so it cannot breach the #628 anti-circularity contract). No new quantity needs minting. And NO schema change is needed: the store row's PK already includes 'class' and the builder already emits one row per class, so the per-class value simply replaces the repeated scalar in an existing per-class slot.

questions.question: What law scales the whole-lap grip σ down to a per-class band width — (A) time-share-linear, (B) sqrt-share, (C) grip-sensitivity weighting, or (D) deficit-proportional?
questions.resolution: (A) time-share-linear: σ⁺_c = s_c · σ_session with s_c = ClassTimeLedger.time_share_by_class. Grip is a session-level COMMON-MODE effect (one curve per year/gp/session), so it perturbs all classes of one lap coherently; under perfect correlation per-part uncertainties add linearly, giving the coherence identity Σ_c σ⁺_c = σ_session that mirrors the point-side identity Σ_c time_deficit_c = lap_time_deficit_s. Given normalised weights, linear share-weighting is the unique law satisfying it. (B) is the independent-errors composition — wrong correlation model, and it over-widens exactly the small classes the bug hurts most. (D) makes the width depend on the quantity it bounds (a #628-flavoured circularity). (C) is physically better but mints a per-class grip weighting G does not carry — that is 're-fitting G', explicitly out of #690 scope → routed to triage. @grade: guess · leans g2 · settle: recompute the #670 held-out coverage/log-score under (A) vs (B)

questions.question: Time shares from the driver's REAL lap (driver-specific width) or the constructor's IDEAL lap (width identical for team-mates)?
questions.resolution: The driver's REAL lap. The band's location is that class's own transit-time deficit, whose time base is where the real lap actually spent its seconds; the ideal lap's shares would mismatch the location being wrapped. v_real is already in hand, so no new input. Alternative recorded as the knob if a later consumer needs team-mate-identical widths. @grade: guess · leans g2 · settle: compare per-class shares from v_real vs v_ideal on one weekend; if max |Δs_c| < 0.01 the choice is immaterial

questions.question: The store column g_sigma_onesided keeps its name and type but changes MEANING. Bump driver_class_observables format_version?
questions.resolution: Yes, bump it — conditional on a verification task first. A store mixing vintages would feed fit.py a silent mixture of two semantics into sigma_cell, precisely the project's named silent-wrongness failure mode; format_version is the existing persisted mechanism, so nothing new is minted. The gate's first task greps every reader of format_version and confirms a bump neither breaks reads nor is silently ignored; the fallback (schema-comment change plus an explicit rebuild note) is stated rather than pretending the vintage is marked. @grade: guess · leans g3 · settle: grep readers of format_version on driver_class_observables
